params.body:
## What was wrong

`ArchivingAReportTest::the_controller_and_the_archive_make_the_same_sheet` renders one report twice, once through the controller and once through the archive, and compares the two PDFs after removing what may differ between two renders. #275 changed no report, and it went red on this test.

The sheet comes from Chrome (`/Producer (Skia/PDF m156)`), not from dompdf as the comment said. Chrome numbers every element of the PDF's structure tree as `(node00000093)`, and two renders need not start that count at the same place. The test removed the number only after `/ID`, not the places the same number comes back: the `/Headers` of a table cell, and the tree's `/Names` and `/Limits`. On #275 the two sheets were the same apart from every node number being one higher in the second:

```
-/Headers [(node00000093)]>> <</O /Table
+/Headers [(node00000094)]>> <</O /Table
```

## What changes

`withoutDates` now renumbers the node numbers in the order they appear, instead of removing them. Two renders that start counting at different points compare equal, and a cell that points at another header still fails. The comment now names Chrome. Only this test file changes.

## Checked

On a real sheet saved from the test:

| Comparison | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| Controller sheet vs archived sheet | same | same |
| Archived sheet with every node number one higher (the #275 failure) | different | same |
| Archived sheet with one cell pointing at the next header | | different |

The archiving tests (10) pass with the Chrome renderer on the workbench. The full suite with Chrome has 2 failures, both from the workbench itself: BuildStamp in a worktree, and PrintCheck, which expects the version string of a full Chrome and gets the headless shell's.
params.title: Compare archived sheets without depending on Chrome's node numbers
